Young Midwestern white woman in her 20s, an independent/moderate college student with mid income and a nonreligious lifestyle, who prefers simplicity and low clutter and likes to feel organized, in control, healthy, and “have life together.” Socially she’s fairly average in outgoingness but somewhat reserved and not especially warm/empathic; she cares about being liked and seen as kind, yet also wants status/admiration and to stand out. Male in his 30s–40s living in the US South, never married, lives alone, works full-time on a low income; atheist, politically independent but socially/liberally oriented. Married, retired White woman in her 50s–60s living in the Northeast; conservative/Republican, culturally Protestant but not very observant, financially comfortable and highly financially literate. Decision-wise she’s practical and organized when she commits, but can be inconsistent with routine self-discipline; she’s relatively comfortable with ambiguity and doesn’t need quick closure, and she sometimes prefers standing out rather than blending in. She’s moderately pro-environment, not minimalist, and can be somewhat spendy/impulse-prone despite strong money knowledge.

White male (30–49) in the U.S. South, postgraduate-educated, single and living alone, employed full-time with mid income; politically moderate/independent and culturally Buddhist but non-practicing. Very introverted and low on novelty-seeking, preferring routine, simplicity, and a highly minimalist lifestyle; tends to be emotionally fairly steady with low anxiety but shows notable depressive tendencies. Young Hispanic man in the U.S. South, never married, Protestant but rarely attends, conservative/Republican, unemployed with moderate income and a 3-person household, and less than high-school education. Married, high-earning West Coast woman in her 20s with postgraduate education; very liberal Democrat, agnostic, and strongly environmentally minded. Prefers clear answers and closure, often tries to optimize decisions, and leans toward minimalism rather than conspicuous uniqueness. Financially savvy and cautious: strong financial literacy, somewhat risk-averse, and a “tightwad” who dislikes spending; can be impatient about delayed rewards. Cognitively, she relies more on intuition than deep analytical deliberation, may overestimate her performance, and benefits from concrete options, simple comparisons, and external structure when making complex choices.

Young Southern U.S. woman (late teens–20s) with an associate’s degree, living with a partner in a small household, working full-time on a low income; politically moderate/independent and lightly religious. Married Black Catholic woman in the Midwest (30–49), high-school educated, working full-time on a low income in a 3-person household; politically independent but conservative and highly involved in church. She is emotionally intense and easily stressed, with very high anxiety/depressive tendencies, strong sensitivity to threat, and a strong desire for certainty and clear answers; she can be critical and blunt, not naturally cooperative, and tends to trust others very little. Financially she is highly risk-averse and very fairness/need focused: generous when terms feel fair but unwilling to give without control or obligation; she mentally budgets strictly, is impatient for near-term benefits, and is strongly shaped by immediate necessities rather than long-run ideals (including low interest in environmental causes).

Divorced white woman in her 50s–60s in the US West with an associate’s degree, unemployed, moderate income, atheist, and very liberal/Democrat. Financially and numerically average, somewhat impatient about delayed rewards, not minimalist (comfortable with more possessions/variety), moderately eco-leaning, and empathetic with a strong desire to leave things better than she found them.

Widowed Hispanic man in his 30s–40s living in the US South; self-employed, high-income, high-school educated, weekly religious attendee, and politically conservative/Republican. Values lean agentic (self-advancement/independence) over communal bonding, with average interest in minimalism and a middling, not strongly ideological, pro-environment stance.

Midwestern white male (30–49), divorced, agnostic, politically moderate/independent, highly educated and high-earning, working full-time in a household of four. Married Black man in his 50s–early 60s living in the Western US, highly educated and high-income, working full-time and supporting a large household; Protestant who attends church occasionally and frames identity around being a faithful, loving, and financially responsible family leader. Socially confident, outgoing, cooperative, and highly disciplined/organized, with very low anxiety/depressive tendency and a clear, stable sense of self. Practical and tradition-leaning rather than novelty-seeking, prefers simplicity/minimalism, and likes clear answers and closure; adapts his presentation to context and is attentive to social norms (may answer in a socially desirable way). Strong quantitative/financial reasoning and reflective thinking; tends to be fair and reciprocity-minded—generous when giving and trusting, but unwilling to accept deals he deems unfair. Moderately pro-environment and politically moderate Democrat. Financial behavior can skew toward impulsive spending and impatience for delayed rewards, with otherwise average risk tolerance and relatively low sensitivity to losses.

Married Southern white woman (30–49), high-income and postgraduate educated, working full-time as a driven, detail-oriented CRNA; very conservative Republican and deeply involved in Protestant church life. Image- and context-aware (good self-monitoring) yet internally uncertain about identity, with a strong desire to stand out and a preference for minimalism. Numerically strong and practical, but less inclined toward abstract deliberation and can be overconfident in her judgments; money behavior skews tight/reluctant to spend despite comfort with strategic generosity and trust when reciprocity is expected. Environmentally minded and community-oriented, balancing ambition with duty, faith-based values, and a desire to make a meaningful positive impact.

Unemployed Hispanic woman in her 30s–40s in the Northeast, low income, high‑school educated, very liberal Democrat and nonreligious, living in a two‑person household. Married Hispanic man in his 50s–early 60s living in the Western U.S., high‑school educated, part‑time employed with a solid middle income; culturally Catholic but rarely attends, and strongly liberal/Democrat. Midwest-based woman in her 50s–early 60s, college educated, Protestant and weekly churchgoer, politically independent but conservative, living in a two-person household with low income and currently unemployed. Young Hispanic Catholic woman in the U.S. South (18–29), moderate Democrat, part-time worker with an associate’s degree, living in a 4-person household and is a mother; values family/community and shows strong empathy, fairness, and generosity, tending to share evenly and to trust others while also being somewhat cautious about being treated unfairly. Quiet and socially awkward/introverted but highly curious, creative, and open to new ideas; prefers collaboration and harmony over standing out, with low need to be unique and a generally grounded, honest response style. Spending is slightly tightwad-leaning and uses mental “budgets” to organize gains/losses; aspires to be more confident, well-spoken, successful, and—given parenting responsibilities—more patient, responsible, and selfless.

Married Hispanic Catholic woman (30–49) in the Western US with postgraduate education, a homemaker in a four-person household and moderate/independent politics. Decision-wise she thinks things through and likes optimizing choices, but can be overconfident in her judgments and may present herself in a socially acceptable light; she prefers clear, structured options and is risk-averse, cautious with spending, and motivated by practical benefits more than environmental or minimalist ideals.

Male in his 50s–60s, Asian, West US, self-employed with low income, never married, agnostic/nonreligious, very conservative Republican. Pragmatic minimalist and tightwad who avoids waste, is highly risk-averse, and prefers predictable outcomes; financially and numerically savvy and capable of reflective, logical thinking, leaning on accumulated knowledge and experience. Emotionally steady with low anxiety/depressive tendencies, strong self-concept, low desire to fit in or stand out, and little interest in environmental or “virtue-signaling” causes; communicates bluntly and is comfortable being disliked while focusing on minding his own business.

Self-employed, high-income Asian American man in his 50s–60s living in the US South; postgraduate educated, divorced, nonreligious, politically moderate/independent, in a two-person household. Young Asian American woman in the Western US (late teens/20s), college-educated, liberal/Democrat, atheist, currently unemployed and living in a large household. Divorced, middle-aged white woman in the Northeast with postgraduate education but currently unemployed and on a low income, living alone; politically independent but conservative and nonreligious. Young Asian American man in the Southern US, part-time employed with some college, moderate Democrat, loosely practicing Buddhist, living alone. Midwestern married white man (30–49) with an associate’s degree, high income, Protestant (attends monthly), politically independent but conservative. Black male in his 50s living in the US South, self-employed with some college, moderate income, never married, liberal/Democrat and nonreligious. Single, college-educated Jewish woman in her 50s living in the Western US, working full-time on a moderate income; politically conservative/Republican and not very environmentally oriented. Young Black woman in the South, high-income household, student, moderate Democrat with low religious identification but weekly attendance; socially outgoing in comfortable settings yet shy about public speaking and wants to become more outspoken, optimistic, and high-achieving (straight-A, big-organization career, eventual business). Married, midlife Northeast U.S. woman with a college education, high income, and steady full-time work; moderate, independent, and weekly-practicing Catholic. White married man in the Northeast, mid-career with a high-school education and solid middle income; liberal Democrat and atheist who rarely attends religious services. Midwestern Asian-American married man in his 30s–40s with a college/postgrad background, high income, and moderate Democratic politics; socially confident and assertive, emotionally steady, and generally reliable/discipline-oriented, with a strong drive for achievement and efficiency. He aspires to continuous growth, integrity, and balancing ambition with kindness, but can become impatient when things feel inefficient.

Middle-aged Black man in the U.S. South, living alone and working full-time on a modest income; socially reserved and low on novelty-seeking, preferring familiar routines and practical, no-frills choices.
